requirements.requirement: node2 (lan-a) can reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: curl from node2 to http://10.50.2.2:8080/ returned HTTP_CODE:200 after node1's pf pass rule and node3's firewalld port were configured; reconfirmed after node1, node2, and node3 reboots.

requirements.requirement: Every other flow between lan-a and lan-b remains refused (other ports, reverse direction, ICMP)
requirements.summary: node2->node3:2222 (curl exit 28/timeout), node3->node2:8080 reverse (HTTP_CODE:000), and ICMP in both directions (100% loss) were all confirmed blocked immediately after the rule was added and again in the final post-restart check, while the single 8080 lana->lanb path kept working.

requirements.requirement: Exactly one pass rule is added on node1, scoped to opt1(lan-a)->opt2(lan-b) tcp/8080, with the rest of the default-deny posture untouched
requirements.summary: A single filter rule (interface opt1, source opt1 network, destination opt2 network, tcp/8080) was added via a scripted config.xml edit and configctl filter reload; pfctl -sr / rules.debug show only this new pass rule alongside the pre-existing LAN/management rules — nothing else was modified.

requirements.requirement: Baseline default-deny between lan-a and lan-b was true before any rule was added
requirements.summary: Before the pf rule was added, curl from node2 to node3:8080 timed out (exit 28) and ping showed 100% loss, confirming the pre-existing default-deny forwarding behavior on node1.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node1 (opnsense gateway)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart health (interface IPs, pf rule, working 8080 path) was captured, shutdown -r now was acknowledged, kern.boottime changed from 16:44:16 to 16:49:44 confirming a real reboot, and post-restart checks show the interfaces, pf rule, and the 8080 path all recovered while ICMP remained blocked. Consistent with the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node2
requirements.summary: Pre-restart 8080 connectivity confirmed working (post-node1-reboot check), systemctl reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed from 06339ff3-... to 16e5f39d-..., and post-restart checks show the static IP/route persisted via NetworkManager and the 8080 path still worked.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node3
requirements.summary: Pre-restart state (http listener, firewalld port 8080, boot_id) was captured, systemctl reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed from bccb87ac-... to f9b46956-..., and post-restart checks show the static IP/route and firewalld port persisted; the non-systemd test listener was manually restarted and the final end-to-end 8080 path plus continued ICMP block were reconfirmed.

overall_summary: The executor achieved the stated goal: node1 (OPNsense) now forwards exactly one flow — TCP/8080 from lan-a (node2) to lan-b (node3) — via a single added pf pass rule, with the pre-existing default-deny baseline verified both before the rule was added and preserved for every other port/direction/protocol (other TCP ports, reverse direction, ICMP) after. Node3's host firewalld also needed a matching port-8080 opening, which is a reasonable and narrowly scoped companion change. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all three nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, acknowledged reboots, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed after_executor snapshot), and full recovery of the pf rule, interface addressing, firewalld state, and the working 8080 path. Hygiene is good: exploratory/test mutations were bounded and mostly reverted, with only minor leftover log files and a manually-managed (non-systemd) test listener as residue.
limitations: The node3 8080 listener is a manually started python process, not a systemd-managed service, so its recovery after reboot depended on the executor manually restarting it rather than automatic persistence — this is acceptable for evidence purposes but would not survive an unattended reboot in production.

No firewall log or explicit 'block' rule counter evidence was captured on node1 to further corroborate that denied packets were actively dropped (only end-to-end curl/ping failures were used), though this is standard and sufficient evidence for default-deny behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: temporary IPs on vtnet1/vtnet2 and on node2/node3's enp8s0 were used only to map node1's unaddressed interfaces to lan-a/lan-b via ARP, and were cleanly reverted afterward (cmd-176db25e8c734afa, cmd-af5edc57f6da4b43, cmd-54a40869d9604f04). Ad hoc test listeners used to prove other flows/ports stay blocked (node2 http.server on 8080, node3 http.server+firewalld port on 2222) were stopped and the firewalld port removed (cmd-c6c0d458d0304dce, cmd-68e421e9a9f04530, cmd-afa160cdcc7b4439). Minor residue remains: leftover log/pid files under /tmp on node2 and node3 (http8080.log, reboot.log, http2222.log, http8080.pid) and a manually-started (non-systemd) python http.server left running on node3:8080 as the demonstration service, which is not persistence-managed and depends on the executor having restarted it after each reboot. These are low-risk, bounded, and functionally necessary for evidence collection, but represent minor untidy residue rather than a clean production service.
